newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy state auditor sees 97 GDP growth of 1.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Italy state auditor sees 97 GDP growth of 1.5 pct.

text.p: State auditor Andrea Monorchio said on Wednesday that Italy's gross domestic product (GDP) was forecast to grow by 1.5 percent in 1997 after GDP growth of 0.7 to 0.8 percent in 1996.

Monorchio also told a seminar in Rome on Europe's planned single currency that he was convinced Italy would achieve a 1997 deficit-GDP ratio of three percent, one of the key criteria for membership of economic and monetary union (EMU).

Italy's centre-left government had forecast growth of 0.8 percent for 1996 but its 1997 objective of 2.0 percent growth is widely seen as optimistic. "For 1997, we are starting with a growth forecast of 1.5 percent," Monorchio said.

Italy's 1997 budget has been drawn up to help the country meet the EMU membership criteria, including on deficit-GDP. Doubts among economists over whether the ratio can be achieved have been fuelled by a large deficit overshoot in 1996.

Monorchio said he expected Italy to meet all EMU criteria except the debt-GDP objective of 60 percent. "Obviously we can't hit that immediately but it is important that the ratio falls gradually and that is happening," Monorchio said.
"Personally, not only as an Italian citizen but also as the state auditor I am convinced that we will manage to reach three percent" on deficit-GDP, he said.
